title: Marienfeld Monastery - Teuto-Navigator
content: Founded in 1185, the Cistercian monastery of Marienfeld was one of the most important monasteries in Westphalia until its dissolution in 1803, and its spiritual influence was widely felt in the Westphalian region. An outstanding example of Cistercian architecture is the late Romanesque abbey church, whose architecture had a lasting influence on other important church buildings in the Westphalia region and the Baltic Sea area. Together with the baroque abbey building, which borders the church to the west, the old abbey church characterizes the old farmyard of the former monastery. To the east and west, this is dominated by the farm buildings built in the first half of the 18th century, making the entire monastery courtyard an oasis of peace and relaxation. In addition, the 1200-metre-long Cistercian Trail offers a historical tour around the monastery grounds. The 618-year-old history of the monastery is vividly explained on 13 steles. The monastery can be visited as part of a guided tour.

title: Archaeologists Were Digging in a Town Center—And Found a 600-Year-Old Christian Monastery
content: 3. Archaeologists Were Digging in a Town Center—And Found a 600-Year-Old Christian Monastery. The thick monastery walls were preserved beneath rubble that collected over the centuries. * A development project in the town center of Borken, in western Germany, revealed the well-preserved remains of a monastery. In the town’s Brinkerhof neighborhood, archaeologists uncovered the remains of the 15th-century Marienbrink monastery church. The walls were four feet thick and over five feet tall, often buried beneath layers of thick rubble that helped preserve the ancient foundation as the city grew and expanded over it. The High Middle Ages site likely stood close to the parish church of St. Remigius, which was built around 800 C.E. The monastery was dissolved in the early 19th century, but parts of the complex were repurposed in 1818 for a Jewish center consisting of a synagogue, school, and ritual bath, or *mikveh*. The fact that the Marienbrink monastery was built in the center of Borken helped to preserve the hidden foundation of the monastery, even after its dissolution.

title: Medieval monastery remains discovered beneath Borken's ...
content: # Medieval monastery remains discovered beneath Borken’s historic center in Germany. Archaeologists have been working for months in the historic center of Borken, where a new health center and Caritas building are planned in the Brinkerhof quarter. The highlight of the preliminary investigations: the massive and well-preserved foundations of the church of the former Marienbrink Monastery from the Late Middle Ages. During this phase, archaeologists encountered the first clear remains of the former Marienbrink Monastery church. In 2024, the team identified a World War II air raid bunker southwest of the church remains. In 1818, a synagogue with an adjoining school and a mikveh was established on the grounds, reusing parts of the older complex.
